To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
audit quality is negatively associated with innovation.

Audit quality is negatively associated with firm innovation, and the negative association is robust to alternative measures of innovation, alternative measures of auditor quality and alternative measures of endogeneity.
audit quality, measured by the likelihood of an audit opinion change and the number of Big 4 auditors, is associated with lower technological innovation, measured by patent output.

the effects of audit quality and the implications for firm innovation.

high audit quality has an unintended negative effect on innovation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high audit quality, which is generally perceived as a desirable attribute, has an unintended effect of reducing firm innovation.
audit quality, which is often considered as the gold standard of accounting quality, may have a negative effect on firm performance.

The main takeaway from our work is that
high audit quality can have negative effects.
high quality auditors may be too effective in their efforts to improve financial reporting and, in the process, may be inadvertently discouraging managers from pursuing long term growth.
high audit quality can be detrimental to firm innovation and, in turn, to the economy.
